samples.question: The picture shows one square sheet ruled into a 4 by 4 grid of square tiles, with four small brightly coloured squares sitting exactly on the four corners of the sheet. Each tile is ruled into 3 by 3 equal cells and carries exactly two things: one solid dark block, which fills a two by two square of cells parked in one of the tile's four corners, and one small brightly coloured notch, which sits in the tile's border strip at the middle of exactly one of the tile's four edges. Every tile has already been turned in place about its own centre by some quarter turn, and its notch was carried around by that same turn. Undo it: turn each tile about its own centre, without moving it out of its place in the grid, until that tile's notch is back at the middle of the tile's top edge, which carries the block to a new corner of the tile. When all sixteen tiles have been turned this way, the sixteen blocks show one of these five arrangements: quads (every block sits in the corner of its tile nearest the centre of the sheet, so the blocks meet in fours to make four large solid squares, one in each quarter of the sheet), window (every block sits in the corner of its tile furthest from the centre of the sheet, so all sixteen blocks stay separate and a wide empty cross is left through the middle of the sheet), grid (every block sits at the top left corner of its own tile, making an evenly spaced array of sixteen separate blocks), bars (the blocks meet in vertical pairs, the first and second tile rows joining and the third and fourth tile rows joining, with every block against the left hand edge of its tile, making eight upright bars), dashes (the blocks meet in horizontal pairs, the first and second tile columns joining and the third and fourth tile columns joining, with every block against the top edge of its tile, making eight flat bars). A few tiles may sit on the wrong corner; take the arrangement that the sixteen turned blocks match most closely. Which arrangement do the turned blocks form? Answer with one word.
